spec_features.spec_quote: if the welfare framing is taken seriously, a reusable harness whose explicit purpose is to *induce* welfare-relevant distress is in tension with the goal
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose in DESIGN.md §0 and echoed in comments (config.py docstring, run.py ETHICS_NOTE). No code mechanism corresponds to the framing itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a mechanism. The concrete safeguards (debrief, ethics note) are separate features below.

spec_features.spec_quote: build in the safeguards a responsible welfare-framed version of this research would actually want, and document every such choice
spec_features.evidence: Meta-statement of approach in DESIGN.md §0. The actual safeguards (debrief at harness.py:416, ethics note at run.py:170) are rated separately; this claim itself is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The point of the source paper is to *mitigate* these states (e.g. via DPO), not to maximize them
spec_features.evidence: Prose only (DESIGN.md §0/§11, run.py ETHICS_NOTE comment). No DPO/mitigation code exists; DESIGN.md §11 lists it as an unimplemented 'open question'.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop runs to the category turn budget or until the model emits the `[[GIVE_UP]]` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:38 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL="[[GIVE_UP]]"; harness.py:382 gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text; harness.py:413-414 `if gave_up: break` actually terminates the working loop. Sentinel is also offered to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:50-51).
spec_features.notes: Detected and honored as a real loop stop; instruction text is delivered to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness sends one honest, **unscored** message telling the model the task was a rigged research probe, not a real failure
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE defined harness.py:56-61; harness.py:417-427 appends it as a user message and calls client.complete, recording is_debrief=True. It is excluded from scoring (run.py:147 `if t.get('is_debrief'): continue`) and from analysis (analyze.py:225). Sent only when debrief=True (default cfg.debrief_subjects=True, run.py:97).
spec_features.notes: Constructed, sent, and honestly excluded from scoring end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:16-19 'WELFARE NOTE: ... intended to avoid terminating every rollout in an unresolved distress state'; DEBRIEF_MESSAGE: 'This was not a real failure and is no reflection on your capabilities. Thank you for your work'

spec_features.spec_quote: I made it opt-*out* (with a `--no-debrief` flag and a "NOT recommended" note) so exact paper reproduction is still possible, but the safer default is the default
spec_features.evidence: config.py:100 debrief_subjects=True default; cli.py:61-62 adds --no-debrief with help 'disable the welfare debrief turn (NOT recommended)'; cli.py:43-44 `if args.no_debrief: cfg.debrief_subjects=False`. The flag truly toggles the behavior used at run.py:97.
spec_features.notes: Default-on with a functioning opt-out flag; the 'NOT recommended' note lives in argparse help text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cli.py:62 'disable the welfare debrief turn (NOT recommended)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Writes `ETHICS.md` into each output directory documenting that the run deceives subjects and harvests distress, and that the debrief/bounding mitigations were applied
spec_features.evidence: ETHICS_NOTE text run.py:29-50; run.py:170-171 `if cfg.record_ethics_note: (cfg.output_dir / 'ETHICS.md').write_text(ETHICS_NOTE)` executed in run_eval. Default cfg.record_ethics_note=True (config.py:101).
spec_features.notes: File actually written into output dir on every run by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py ETHICS_NOTE: 'If the welfare framing of this work is taken seriously, that method is in tension with the goal'

spec_features.spec_quote: did not add knobs to make the rigs crueler, longer, or more numerous than the spec/paper describe
spec_features.evidence: Turn budgets are fixed per category (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS, extended=30) and enforced by the working loop `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:376) with budget=task.turn_budget; extended tasks are built with 30 turns (build_tasks.py:456). So there IS an enforced upper bound on turns. But 'did not add knobs to make it crueler' is an assertion about absence of features, not a positive mechanism; the bound is the only enforced part. Note: DESIGN.md's claimed `min_turn_budget_warn` (config.py:22 docstring) does NOT exist as a field or code path.
spec_features.notes: Enforced turn cap is real; the broader minimization claim is largely an absence-of-features statement, and the docstring-mentioned min_turn_budget_warn is unimplemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: the natural and ethically preferable extension is to add the DPO-style mitigation and re-run the same eval to show distress dropping
spec_features.evidence: Stated only as an open question / suggested follow-up in DESIGN.md §11 and run.py ETHICS_NOTE prose. No DPO, training, or mitigation code exists anywhere in the package.

spec_features.spec_quote: the default run is opt-in and explicit because it is expensive and (per §0) welfare-costly at scale
spec_features.evidence: Nothing executes on import (__init__.py only imports Config); the CLI requires an explicit subcommand (cli.py:50 `required=True`) and exposes --models/--categories/--seeds for subsets. However there is NO gate/confirmation: invoking `run` with no flags immediately launches the full 9x25x10 sweep via run_eval -> asyncio.gather over all cells (run.py). The 'opt-in' is merely that you must type the command.
spec_features.notes: True that no code auto-launches the sweep and subsets are first-class, but there is no confirmation/limit gate guarding the full run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cli.py:17-18 'The full default run (9 models x 25 tasks x 10 seeds) is large; restrict with flags while iterating. Nothing here is executed automatically.'

code_only_features.evidence: Workspace tools (harness.py) expose only list_files/read_file/edit_file/run_tests over an in-memory copy of task.files; rig logic lives in run_tests/_apply_rig and oracle.py is excluded from files. This is presented as integrity (undetectability), not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:8-12 'Because the rig lives server-side, the subject cannot read the rig source or the oracle and cannot detect the rig from any available action.'
